Investigator note (LLM): The device fanout lookup reveals that the shared Chrome 66.0 device profile appears across multiple distinct cards within short time windows, indicating broader browser fingerprint reuse. Several associated transactions show elevated model scores, consistent with automated card testing patterns across multiple accounts. The cardholder's history of 18 prior confirmed fraud cases establishes a baseline vulnerability for card-not-present exploitation. No remaining uncertainties affect the classification of this transaction as unauthorized fraud.

case.summary: This case was triggered by customer C13171 reporting an unauthorised $55.68 online purchase on card C13171-K2 via message: 'I never made this $55.68 purchase. Please check my card.' Refers to 3558054. The graph showed a burst of online transactions on the same card within 48 hours and connections to other cards sharing the same device profile. The verdict is fraud with an initial and final fraud probability of 0.99, supported by the cardholder report and case memory models. Actions taken include automatically creating the case, automatically monitoring connected cards, recommending block card under L1, and recommending filing a report under L2 pending approval.

sar.narrative: Customer C13171 reported an unauthorised online transaction on card C13171-K2. The suspicious activity occurred on December 19, 2016, via the online channel using device profile ' |  | chrome 66.0 | '. The transactions involved a burst of online purchases on card C13171-K2 totaling $166.97, specifically transactions 3557979 ($55.60), 3557987 ($55.69), and 3558054 ($55.68). This activity is suspicious because the cardholder denies the purchases, the case-memory model gives the transaction a calibrated fraud rate of 69.9% with a score of 0.951, and the activity connects to a shared device profile linked to fraud on other cards such as C11642-K1. The total exposure amount is $166.97. Actions taken include automatically creating the case and monitoring connected cards, while blocking the card and filing a report are recommended actions awaiting human approval under L1 and L2 respectively.
